name: YourStory

sources.title: Companies section — startup profiles on India's largest startup-media platform
Catalogued submission URL — a Google Form (returns auth-required to non-JS fetches)
Backmit profile — asks for account, company name, live website URL
Third-party guide — claims free submission; fields: name, URL, 60-char tagline, 250-char description, 512px+ square logo, 2–3 screenshots, pricing model

requirements: Startup/company profile for YourStory's companies directory — India-focused startup media
Submission goes through a Google Form — a Google account may be required to fill it
Third-party sources list required assets: product name, live URL, ~60-char tagline, ~250-char description, square logo >=512px, 2–3 screenshots, pricing model
Editorial selection applies — this is a media property, not a guaranteed listing
preparation: Tagline (~60 chars), description (~250 chars), square logo >=512px, 2–3 screenshots, pricing model
Founder details and India-relevance angle if applicable
workflow: Open the catalogued Google Form URL in a signed-in browser
Complete all fields (reported as all-required; the form rarely saves drafts — have everything ready)
Submit and wait for editorial review — no stated SLA
If accepted, a company profile appears under yourstory.com/companies
watchFor: The form is Google-Forms-hosted — needs a browser and possibly a Google login; it 401s to automated fetches
Sources conflict on cost (one says free, another says paid listing) — treat pricing as unverified
Link type conflicts across sources (dofollow vs nofollow) — don't count on the SEO value
Editorial gate: YourStory is a media outlet, so boring/non-Indian-market submissions may simply go unanswered
Don't confuse this with Tech30/brand-partnership programs, which are separate application paths
countsAsLive: Company profile page exists under yourstory.com/companies/<slug> with description and link
unknowns: Whether submission is currently free or paid — sources conflict
Whether the profile link is dofollow or nofollow — sources conflict
